doc.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Closing words and thanks
summary: Rowe reads back Tolliver's earlier quotes, they discuss the pandemic and the Strata-East event, and say goodbye.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: I’ll wrap up, this is like a tag on a good jazz tune I think. I picked out some things that you said in our first session that I thought were marvelous and put them into a paragraph for you. So this is Charles Tolliver: “Once I realized I could do something with this art form I just wanted to belong. It’s a glorious adventure, my life’s work. I have not a nanosecond of regret. I am my grandmother and mother. You finish what you start.”
So I want to thank you for starting and keeping going.

Thank you. We just got to keep our health, I mean we manage to get past this mother of all pandemics in our lifetime, so hopefully we’re going to be okay and get some music up to the Utica area of the country.
That would be really nice. I’ll see what I can do about that.
Thank you very much and I hope your Strata-East event is fulfilling and goes very well.
Well share it with your constituents — as Charlie Parker said, my worthy constituents from Massey Hall — and hopefully they’ll try to get themselves into the virtual audience.
Yup. All right Mr. Tolliver, thank you again for your time. It’s been a real pleasure.
